notes.text: No authorial page number is visible at the top; a pale lower-left foliation reads 59. The line count includes the short lower-right continuation of the Im parenthesis as its own physical row. The manuscript opens On voit alors que, followed by an implication involving x, y and z. It then chooses u and v in a Sigma expression with a visibly lowered local mark. The first p_1 has reworked strokes over its head, and a short brace lies beneath the gap between the two middle equalities. These local marks are retained without assigning an earlier letter from the expected formula.

The author invokes the carré cartésien de (38), writes a cancelled existence expression with a doubtful two-lobed variable, and continues with an existence sign followed by one uninterrupted upright. The upright is transcribed literally; no uniqueness meaning is supplied. The author then writes w=s′(d) and two equality chains. The second chain includes b(s′(d))=b(b′(d)) as written. Neither the referenced square nor the validity of these chains has been independently checked in this page reading.

The conclusion w:x ... z uses a drawn two-arm curved mark whose lower arm ends in an arrowhead. The manuscript next gives x not-prec x and an Im expression with source Sigma_1, label (p_1; underlined b), a visibly unheaded shaft, a crossed product sign and intersection with diag followed by the empty-set sign. The final equality and outer parenthesis continue below at the right. These are descriptions of the source display, without a separate proof of its claim.

The final paragraph describes the relation in the author’s words as the relation d’inégalité stricte associée à une relation d’ordre sur Sigma. It says that Sigma(1) is recovered as the graph and Sigma(2) as the drapeaux x-prec-y-prec-z of length 2, then ends with et les applications. Local raised marks remain doubtful where the ink is compact. A separate curved upright after dans is recorded as an unassigned fragment. No mathematical theorem has been checked during this transcription.
